original_question: Let v be a continuous viscosity supersolution of the local complex Monge-Ampere equation -(dd^c V)^n + f dV = 0 on a bounded domain. If P(v) denotes the plurisubharmonic envelope of v, determine whether P(v) is a pluripotential supersolution of the same equation.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact target. It correctly identifies the local complex Monge-Ampère equation, assumes v is a continuous viscosity supersolution, introduces the plurisubharmonic envelope P(v), and asks the same core open question: whether P(v) should be a pluripotential supersolution of the same equation.
missing_details: The ambient setting is local: Ω is fixed in §6.1 as a bounded pseudoconvex domain in ℂ^n (for example, the unit ball), not just an arbitrary bounded domain.
The coefficient is not arbitrary: §6.2 fixes f ≥ 0 to be a continuous density, and dV is the Euclidean Lebesgue measure.
The paper’s notion of viscosity supersolution is the one from Definition 6.4: for every x ∈ Ω and every C^2 differential test q from below at x, one requires -(dd^c q(x))^n/dV + f(x) ≥ 0.
The envelope should be defined exactly as P(v) := (sup{ψ ∈ PSH(Ω) : ψ ≤ v})*; the upper-semicontinuous regularization is part of the definition.
To make the question stand alone, “pluripotential supersolution” should be spelled out as the Bedford–Taylor pluripotential sense for the psh function P(v), i.e. (dd^c P(v))^n ≤ f dV.
The notation in the equation should consistently use v, not V.
The paper emphasizes that this is a specifically local viscosity/pluripotential issue in §6.2, not a compact Kähler-manifold problem.
refined_question: Let Ω ⊂ ℂ^n be a bounded pseudoconvex domain, let f ≥ 0 be a continuous density, and let dV denote the Euclidean Lebesgue measure. Suppose v: Ω → ℝ is continuous and is a viscosity supersolution of -(dd^c v)^n + f dV = 0 in the sense that for every x ∈ Ω and every C^2 function q defined near x with (v - q)(x) = inf(v - q) near x, one has -(dd^c q(x))^n/dV + f(x) ≥ 0. If P(v) := (sup{ψ ∈ PSH(Ω) : ψ ≤ v})* is the plurisubharmonic envelope of v, must P(v) be a Bedford–Taylor pluripotential supersolution of the same equation, i.e. must it satisfy (dd^c P(v))^n ≤ f dV on Ω in the pluripotential sense?
justification: The draft is targeting Question 40 almost verbatim. The paper first fixes the local setting for §6.1–6.2 (bounded pseudoconvex Ω ⊂ ℂ^n), then in §6.2 fixes f ≥ 0 continuous and dV Euclidean Lebesgue measure, defines viscosity super/subsolutions in Definition 6.4, introduces the psh envelope P(v), and asks exactly whether P(v) is a pluripotential supersolution of the same equation. The nearby context also explains why this is the sharp formulation: for subsolutions and for continuous solutions there are viscosity/pluripotential equivalences, but the supersolution side is asymmetric and “more delicate to interpret”; the paper only records a positive answer in the C^2-smooth case. Because of that context, the refined question should stay narrowly focused on Question 40 rather than being broadened to a more general viscosity/pluripotential correspondence problem.
